biography.plain_text: Abraham Gosman was an American property entrepreneur who built a healthcare property business by converting mansions into nursing homes. He founded Mediplex and Meditrust, separating care operations from property ownership. After selling Mediplex to Avon, he bought it back, restored profitability and sold it again, this time to Sun Healthcare.

long_biography.plain_text:
Healthcare property entrepreneur Abraham Gosman began with a shoe business, developing an inexpensive method of attaching reptile skins to footwear while studying at the University of New Hampshire. A loan from his mother financed the venture. Its earnings gave him capital to invest beyond manufacturing.

His philanthropy included a gift to Brandeis University for its Sports and Convocation Center. In West Palm Beach, he served as a life trustee of the Kravis Center for the Performing Arts. He donated $1 million towards building the Gosman Amphitheater, an outdoor performance venue.
